\section[a aplicação]{a aplicação — the app, the application (software); the use}

\label{lesson:PT-C396-aplicacao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to go bankrupt, then the Portuguese for in debt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a aplicação}
\textbf{a aplicação} — \textquotedblleft{}the app, the application (software); the use\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Descarreguei uma aplicação para aprender línguas.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I downloaded an app for learning languages.}
\end{quote}

In speech \emph{a app}. Also the act of applying: \emph{a aplicação da lei}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{aplicação} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{applicātiō} \textquotedblleft{}attachment, application\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{applicāre} \textquotedblleft{}to join to\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{plicāre} \textquotedblleft{}to fold\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a aplicação}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a aplicação}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a aplicação}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to go bankrupt, then the Portuguese for in debt, then say \emph{a aplicação} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does a aplicação mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The app, the application (software); the use\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[o utilizador]{o utilizador — the user}

\label{lesson:PT-C396-utilizador}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for in debt, then the Portuguese for the app.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o utilizador}
\textbf{o utilizador} — \textquotedblleft{}the user\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A aplicação tem um milhão de utilizadores.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The app has a million users.}
\end{quote}

European Portuguese; in Brazil \emph{o usuário}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{utilizador} is built on \emph{utilizar} \textquotedblleft{}to use\textquotedblright{}, which was borrowed from French \emph{utiliser} (EtymDB); the French verb rests on Latin \emph{ūtilis} \textquotedblleft{}useful\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{ūtī} \textquotedblleft{}to use\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o utilizador}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o utilizador}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o utilizador}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for in debt, then the Portuguese for the app, then say \emph{o utilizador} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[aceder]{aceder — to access, to log in (to)}

\label{lesson:PT-C396-aceder}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the app, then the Portuguese for the user.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: aceder}
\textbf{aceder} — \textquotedblleft{}to access, to log in (to)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Não consigo aceder à minha conta.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I cannot log in to my account.}
\end{quote}

European Portuguese \emph{aceder a}; in Brazil \emph{acessar}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{aceder} comes from Latin \emph{accēdere} \textquotedblleft{}to come near, to approach\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built on \emph{cēdere} \textquotedblleft{}to go\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a senha]{a senha — the password; the (queue) ticket}

\label{lesson:PT-C396-senha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the user, then the Portuguese for to access.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a senha}
\textbf{a senha} — \textquotedblleft{}the password; the (queue) ticket\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Esqueci-me da senha outra vez.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I forgot the password again.}
\end{quote}

Also the number ticket in a queue: \emph{tirar a senha}. \emph{A palavra-passe} is common in Portugal too.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{senha} is inherited from Latin \emph{signa} \textquotedblleft{}signs, marks\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), the plural of \emph{signum} \textquotedblleft{}a sign\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[o perfil]{o perfil — the profile}

\label{lesson:PT-C396-perfil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to access, then the Portuguese for the password.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o perfil}
\textbf{o perfil} — \textquotedblleft{}the profile\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Mudei a foto do meu perfil.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I changed my profile photo.}
\end{quote}

Also the side view of a face.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{perfil} was borrowed from Spanish \emph{perfil} (EtymDB), from Old Provençal \emph{perfil} \textquotedblleft{}outline\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Latin \emph{fīlum} \textquotedblleft{}a thread\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
